questions.stem:
Which of the following set of quantum numbers have same energy?
(a) $n = 2,\ l = 2,\ m = +1$
(b) $n = 2,\ l = 1,\ m = -1$
(c) $n = 3,\ l = 2,\ m = 0$
(d) $n = 3,\ l = 2,\ m = 1$
questions.solution:
(a) $\Rightarrow$ 2d = does not exist
(b) $\Rightarrow$ 2p
(c) $\Rightarrow$ 3d same energy
(d) $\Rightarrow$ 3d same energy

questions.stem: Which of the following has same energy in absence of electric and magnetic field for hydrogen atom?
questions.solution:
For hydrogen atom in absence of electric and magnetic field, energy only depends on principal quantum number(n). For same the value of n, energy will be same
Hence 2s and 2p have same energy.

questions.stem: $\Delta_f H$ of H(g) is 222 kJ/mol, $\Delta_f H$ of O(g) is 250 kJ/mol, $\Delta_f H$ of $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$ is –248 kJ/mol. What is the value of Bond Energy of O – H bond in $\mathrm{H_2O}$ in kJ/mol?
questions.solution:
$$\mathrm{H_2(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}O_2(g) \longrightarrow H_2O(g)}$$
$$\Delta H_f = \sum(\text{B.E. of reactant}) - \sum(\text{B.E. of product})$$
$$-248 = 444 + 250 - (2 \times \text{B.E.}_{\mathrm{O-H}})$$
$$2\text{B.E.}_{\mathrm{O-H}} = 942$$
$$2\text{B.E.}_{\mathrm{O-H}} = 471\ \mathrm{kJ/mole}$$

questions.stem: 70% by mass solution of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ is taken having density 1.41 g/mL. Calculate the molarity of solution
1g of a non-electrolyte solute (MW = 256 g/mol) is dissolved in 50g of solvent, freezing point of solution is lowered by 0.40 K. Calculate the Molal depression constant of solvent.
questions.solution:
$$\Delta T_f = ik_f \times m$$
$$\Delta T_f = i \times k_f \times \frac{W_{solute}}{MW_{solute} \times W_{solvent}} \times 1000$$
$$0.4 = k_f \times \frac{1 \times 1000}{256 \times 50}$$
$$k_f = \frac{0.4 \times 256 \times 50}{1000}$$
$$k_f = 5.12\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$$

questions.stem:
How many of the following ions have same value of spin only magnetic moment?
$\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$
questions.solution:
The ions having same number of unpaired electrons having same value of spin only magnetic moment.
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM (n = Number of unpaired electron)
$\mathrm{Ni^{2+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{8}$, $n = 2$
$\mathrm{V^{2+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{3}$, $n = 3$
$\mathrm{Ti^{2+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{2}$, $n = 2$
$\mathrm{Sc^{3+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{0}$, $n = 0$
$\mathrm{Ti^{3+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{1}$, $n = 1$
$\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ have same value of spin only magnetic moment.
